blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Telemedicine capable for real-time' data sharing back to clinicians assumes a live comms link from point of injury
blind_spots.operator_reality: A combat casualty at point of injury or in a MEDEVAC chain is often in a DDIL environment with no persistent uplink; a device built around continuous real-time telemedicine sync needs a store-and-forward fallback or it goes dark exactly when it matters most
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the product narrative is built around continuous AI monitoring, not intermittent-comms resilience
blind_spots.evidence_quote: utilizes a patented nanosensor array and artificial intelligence algorithms that is telemedicine capable for real-time and rapid detection

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of FDA regulatory clearance status or DoD medical-device/ATO pathway for a wireless sensor handling patient health data on military networks
blind_spots.operator_reality: A wearable diagnostic that wirelessly transmits patient data needs both an FDA pathway and, for DoD use, a data-handling/ATO review before it can touch a military health record system — skipping this is a common reason funded Phase II medtech never reaches a unit
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: team is focused on sensor accuracy and clinical validation milestones, not the regulatory/network-authorization track
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Data can be shared with medical professionals in real-time to realize more accurate and appropriate treatment.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No battery/spares/durability plan for a coin-sized wearable across the evacuation chain (point of injury through hypothermia bag through transport chamber)
blind_spots.operator_reality: A device meant to track a casualty continuously from field to transport needs a charging/battery-swap logistics plan and ruggedization spec; without it, the sensor is dead by the time the patient reaches definitive care
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: marketing emphasizes form factor ('as small as a coin') over power/sustainment logistics
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The RAPID-iNose is small, lightweight, and integrates into wound dressing systems, hypothermia bags, or transport chambers with wirelessly tracking and monitoring of infection development

opener_hook: RAPID-iNose's Phase II abstract calls the device 'telemedicine capable for real-time' data sharing — what's the fallback when the evacuation chain has no uplink back to a clinician?
what_they_do: AI-powered wearable nanosensor that detects wound-infection pathogens in real time from gaseous signatures, originally developed for combat wound monitoring under DoD SBIR funding.
